prompt: Let $R$ be a strict partial order. Which extra condition is necessary and sufficient for it to be a strict total order? All variables range over its domain.

answers.explanation: Together with asymmetry, comparability gives exactly one direction between any two distinct elements.
A strict order cannot have loops on a nonempty domain.
Symmetry and asymmetry together force an empty relation, which is not total on two elements.
This is already assumed; incomparable pairs may remain.
For equal elements this demands a self-loop, contradicting strictness.
Every strict partial order is already antisymmetric.
Every strict partial order is already asymmetric.
Seriality excludes finite strict total orders with a greatest element and does not ensure comparability.
A strict total order on three elements can give the least element two successors.
One related pair does not compare every other pair.
